text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Stocks closed slightly firmer with the support of strong bonds and a sharp advance on Wall Street, but renewed inflation and interest rate fears managed to sour sentiment for much of the day. The FTSE 100 index was encouraged to the day's best levels by the unexpectedly sharp advance on Wall Street. The index finished up 3.6 points at 3,914.4 after trading in negative territory for most of the day.

FRANKFURT - Stocks ended thin market trade lower, taking a break after they reached record highs Friday, with profit-taking and dollar weakness pressuring the market. The DAX index of 30 leading stocks closed market dealings at a day's low of 2,728.32 points, down 11.51 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade in the DAX index, ended down 1.85 points at 2,730.44.

PARIS - The stock market was closed today for a national holiday celebrating the armistice of World War I. On Friday, stocks closed in negative ground after racking up major gains earlier in the week. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,205.20.

ZURICH - Stocks ended higher in quiet trading and on moderate volume, drawing strength from a firming tone in bonds and early advances on Wall Street. The all-share SPI was up 6.20 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,445.86 points.

TOKYO - Stocks settled lower, with their drop eating away at the huge gains they posted late last week. Brokers said outright cash trades were fairly thin and that futures-linked activity was responsible for the fluctuations in the Nikkei average. The 225-issue Nikkei average lost 135.96 points, or 0.64 percent, to land at 21,065.08.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed slightly up, largely on speculative interest in Hongkong Telecom. The Hang Seng Index finished 20.70 points up at 12,771.86 after recovering from an 80-point tumble at the start of the day. Turnover remained robust at HK$6.41 billion but was substantially off Friday's HK$8.42 billion.

SYDNEY - Shares closed slightly lower after a listless trading session. Investors were uninspired by weak leads from offshore markets and there was a lack of local news to drive the market. The All Ordinaries index closed 4 points lower at 2,358.1, off its intraday 2,366.1.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks tumbled on a bleak outlook on various factors, including a presistently high money market shortage, fuelling fears of an interest rate hike. Industrial stocks were hardest hit with the index diving over one percent as futures arbitrage players sold off stock in the spot market. The industrial index shed 99.9 points to 7,891.9, lopping 60.8 points off the all-share index, which finished at 6,732.7. The gold index ended 2.3 points weaker at 1,678.8.
